\section[śāle]{\kn{ಶಾಲೆ} (śāle) — school}

\label{lesson:KA-C92-school}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for home town, then the Kannada for language.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಶಾಲೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಶಾಲೆ}} (\emph{śāle}) — \textquotedblleft{}school\textquotedblright{}.

A \textbf{\kn{ಶಿಕ್ಷಕ}} (\emph{śikṣaka}), \textquotedblleft{}teacher\textquotedblright{}, works in one.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Where the teacher you know works.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śāle}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śāle}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{śāle}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for home town, then the Kannada for language, then say \emph{śāle} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಶಾಲೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}School\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kālēju]{\kn{ಕಾಲೇಜು} (kālēju) — college}

\label{lesson:KA-C92-college}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for language, then the Kannada for school.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕಾಲೇಜು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕಾಲೇಜು}} (\emph{kālēju}) — \textquotedblleft{}college\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from English and given a Kannada ending \textbf{‑\kn{ಉ}} (\emph{-u}), the way Kannada rounds off words that end in a consonant.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An English word in Kannada clothes.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kālēju}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kālēju}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kālēju}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for language, then the Kannada for school, then say \emph{kālēju} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕಾಲೇಜು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}College\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\label{lesson:KA-C92-job}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for college, then the Kannada for office.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಉದ್ಯೋಗ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಉದ್ಯೋಗ}} (\emph{udyōga}) — \textquotedblleft{}job, occupation\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಿಮ್ಮ} \kn{ಉದ್ಯೋಗ} \kn{ಏನು}?} (\emph{nimma udyōga ēnu?}) — \textquotedblleft{}what is your job?\textquotedblright{}

The name question again, asked about work.

\section[iṅgliṣ]{\kn{ಇಂಗ್ಲಿಷ್} (iṅgliṣ) — English (the language)}

\label{lesson:KA-C92-english}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for office, then the Kannada for a job.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಇಂಗ್ಲಿಷ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಇಂಗ್ಲಿಷ್}} (\emph{iṅgliṣ}) — \textquotedblleft{}English\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಇಂಗ್ಲಿಷ್} \kn{ಗೊತ್ತು}} (\emph{nanage iṅgliṣ gottu}) — \textquotedblleft{}I know English\textquotedblright{}, built like \textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಕನ್ನಡ} \kn{ಗೊತ್ತು}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The language you already speak, in Kannada.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṅgliṣ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṅgliṣ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nanage iṅgliṣ gottu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for office, then the Kannada for a job, then say \emph{iṅgliṣ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
